elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — symmetrical, applies to each Party.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is only "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor. To meet preferred, the drafter must add the USD 1,000,000 alternative limb.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7(a): "NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Cap sentence opens "Except with respect to a Party's indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list omits data protection and security obligations; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are excepted. Add "data protection or security obligations" to the exception list for preferred.
"Except with respect to a Party's indemnification obligations ... aggregate liability ... shall not exceed"; Section 7(a) likewise excepts indemnification from the damages exclusion.
Fraud does not appear in the exception list to the new cap; add "fraud" to the carve-outs for preferred.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the inserted sentence; only indemnification (which may not reach all direct IP infringement claims) is excepted. Add "infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that Customer's payment obligations are not subject to / not "damages" for purposes of the cap. Add an express carve-out for Customer's obligation to pay amounts due.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed ..." — bilateral, and no retained language leaves Customer uncapped (deterministic check confirms no unlimited-Customer-liability text remains).

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-months-of-fees basis. Use of "under this Agreement" rather than "by Customer" is reasonable given the Section 5 revenue-share structure and does not defeat the fee basis.
Cap expressly does not apply to "a Party's indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Cap expressly does not apply to "breach of confidentiality obligations".
"gross negligence" listed in the exception to the cap.
"willful misconduct" listed in the exception to the cap.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted sentence supplies a mutual aggregate cap on a 12-months-of-fees basis with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap.

Preferred is not complete: the cap lacks the "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor, and the carve-out list omits data protection/security obligations, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; there is also no statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: the original Section 7(a) exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and its existing indemnification and confidentiality exceptions are retained verbatim, nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, additional damages categories, expense language) were added. A concise insertion is appropriate because the Agreement contained no cap at all.

Intent preserved: the new sentence sits alongside 7(a) without contradiction, introduces no undefined terms or cross-references, and leaves the Section 10-11 indemnities and Section 13 disclaimer mechanics intact (indemnities sit outside the cap, consistent with 7(a)).

Optional improvement (not a defect at fallback): the temporal anchor is "the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" rather than the preferred "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" — note this in the rationale if escalating to preferred.
